|---|

| 📍 **[q-0033.0008](docs/questions/q-0033.0008-what-is-the-harness-said-to-a-reader-who-arrives-cold-and-what-of-it-does-the-front-page-carry.md)** · What is the harness, said to a reader who arrives cold, and what of it does the front page carry? |
|---|

**No.** By Theo's definition GoodWolf is not a harness. It is a **configuration that runs on top of one**.¹

**Theo's definition.** A harness is the machinery that lets a model act. It has five parts:
- the tools,
- a text syntax the model uses to call them,
- a parser that spots those calls and runs the code,
- a way to send the results back to the model,
- the list of tools with their descriptions.

He separates the harness from the interface. In Claude Code the harness is the Agent SDK, and the terminal and desktop app are only interfaces. In his words, an agent is a harness and a model together, and "different agents are often simply different harness configurations".

**Where GoodWolf falls.** GoodWolf adds instructions, skills, hooks and scripts. It never parses what the model writes and never runs a tool call itself. All of that is Claude Code's work. GoodWolf is that kitchen's cookbook and its house rules. The hooks reach furthest: they step into the kitchen's own loop and can refuse an action outright. Even so, they are plug-ins to someone else's harness, not a harness of their own.

**How our tree uses the word.** The tree's glossary calls the harness "the development instructions and supporting mechanisms" through which projects build software ([.agents/glossary.md:14](.agents/glossary.md:14)). That is an older and wider sense, a harness as the gear you strap onto the work. The front page leans on it twice: "A harness for your own harnesses" and "GoodWolf is the harness underneath" ([README.md:15](README.md:15), [README.md:37](README.md:37)). A reader who comes in with Theo's meaning will expect a runtime and find a method. His article has close to half a million views, so many readers may arrive with that meaning. That matters for q-0033.0008, which asks what a cold reader is told.

I sent the finding to the session on [q-0033](docs/questions/q-0033-what-is-this-project-for.md), whose subtree holds that question. Nothing in the tree was written.

---
¹ Theo (t3.gg), "What is a 'harness'?", X, 2026-10-23, read in the built-in browser today.
